correctness.rationale: For syndrome image W, every support of k parity columns spans W. If its first-coordinate functional is nonzero, minimal k=r and all possible supports are unordered all-affine bases of W, giving |GL_r(2)|/((2^r−1)r!) unique solutions. If first syndrome row is zero but S nonzero, k>=r+1; every minimizing support is an affine (r+1)-point basis in one of 2^(m-r) cosets v+W, yielding 2^m|GL_r(2)|/(r+1)! solutions. Uniqueness of coefficients and nonvanishing of each coefficient row are shown. Gaussian rank counts finish the syndrome census. A separate brute-force correction enumerator verified all syndromes for 8 parameter pairs including 4096 syndromes at (3,3). The finite tests supplement, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The established maximum generalized covering radius and the general notion of joint coverings do not determine syndrome-resolved counts of minimal correction matrices. Six semantic published-finding corpus searches and two targeted literature searches, complemented by comparison with the full available 2021/2022 foundations and 2026 rate paper, found no equivalent statement. The proof gives an exact pair (minimum support, number of minimizers) for every binary extended-Hamming syndrome and a complete finite profile. Unindexed earlier geometry and inaccessible recent full text remain specific priority risks, not claims of certainty.
residual_risks: The full 2026 finite-geometric framework of Alfarano et al. was not accessible; an implicit equivalent affine-basis enumeration could be present.
Older coset-leader and multiple-covering literature may contain equivalent scalar and possibly multi-syndrome counting identities; one relevant 1995 paper was accessible only as abstract.
Novelty is a best-knowledge assessment, not a certified or independent claim.

value.rationale: The exact complete joint nearest-cover profile answers the natural question of how many equally optimal access sets an extended Hamming coded system has for multiple simultaneous syndrome constraints. Fixed distance does not determine that multiplicity: same-distance syndromes can have one or 2^m-scale minimizing correction choices. The rank/first-row classification is a uniform all-m,t structural result, with exact populations and a fixed-t asymptotic probability 2^−t of a deep syndrome carrying 2^m |GL_t(2)|/(t+1)! tied optima. No performance or rate gain is asserted.
